standard_prerequisites.name: Saturation of the ordered structure
standard_prerequisites.statement: The system is kappa-saturated as a structure in the language with the ordering, so types over small sets are realised.
standard_prerequisites.use: It produces the element above the subsystem.

standard_prerequisites.name: Binary tree above an element
standard_prerequisites.statement: In an omega-saturated ordered system there is a binary tree of height omega above any element.
standard_prerequisites.use: It supplies the tree that the criterion of the previous proposition needs.

standard_prerequisites.name: Generated subsystem
standard_prerequisites.statement: A = <A> means A is generated by itself.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the hypothesis on the subsystem.

core_obligations: Use saturation to find an element b above the subsystem A (source line 896).
Apply the tree corollary to obtain a binary tree of height omega above b inside the system (source line 896).
Conclude with the criterion of the previous proposition, since the tree witnesses its third condition (source line 896).

proof_roadmap.step: Find an element above the subsystem by saturation.
Build the tree above it and apply the criterion.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled corollary at source lines 894-895: for an infinite unconfined system M, a subset A and an ordering of M that makes M kappa-saturated in the language of the ordering, if the subsystem is generated by A then the closure of A under that ordering is A itself. The proof (source lines 896-897) chains three ingredients: saturation produces an element strictly above A, the tree corollary produces a binary tree of height omega above that element inside M, and the criterion of the preceding proposition then converts the existence of such a tree into the statement about the closure. The corollary records only the closure conclusion.
